main_text.l: HVBERTI LANGVETI AEdui, celebre pietatis, doctrinæ, prudentiæ nomen suis meritis apud Illustr. Germaniæ Principes adepti, amici singularis, Memoriæ.

l.i: Languetii, Lector, Germanis nomen in oris Si quando audisti, fuerim vir qualis habeta. AEdua me genuit tellus, Germania fouit, Isto quinetiam extinctum dignata sepulchro. Si rogitas forsan patria curtam procul alma, Hic iaceam, pepulit certe me patria nunquam, Linquere nec patriam vitium, vel iussit egestas, Sed Pietatis amor, sed magni fama Philippi, Saxonicas haud inuitum perduxit in oras: Hic vbi (Christe, tui, fateor, quod muneris omne est) Principibus, doctisque viris Languetus honeste Transfacta gratus vita, nec inutilis illi Qua me aluit terra, placide post fata quiesco.

main_text.l: NOBILISSIMO ET FORTISSIMO viro, D. Francisco Lanoo, Carmne Epicedium,

l.i: Languum heroem digno exornare sepulcro Tu quicunque Soles [?], paucis hæc, si libet, audi.

page.notes: The scan is cropped at the right edge, so line ends are partly missing (for example "honeste", "vita", "fata", "viris"); the words are read from the visible letters. The initial L of the first verse and the L of the Epicedium are large woodcut-style letters joined to the first word; the first word of each is uncertain ("Languetii" and "Languum" are read with [?] in mind). "Soles" is doubtful and may be "Vales". The top and right of the running head are cut off. "Fac" is the catchword at the lower right, not part of the text.
